Subject: Kernel-aware scaling proposal for Tailwind — renewal planning

Hi Sofia / Tailwind ops team,

Thanks again for the sync last week. Based on Tailwind's steady growth and the telemetry you shared, we've drafted a renewal plan that (a) preserves your low-latency SLO for real-time embedding and chat, (b) reduces unit cost for batch fine-tuning and embeddings by steering those jobs to cheaper kernels, and (c) gives you predictable burst capacity for seasonal spikes.

High-level proposal (attached: tailwind_usage_q1_q2.csv, kernel_profile_summary.pdf):
- Committed pool: 12 H100-class slots reserved for low-latency serving (pin to region us-west-2).
- Flexible compute: 24 mixed-precision A100 slots in a shared tranche for batch/OTF finetunes.
- Kernel-aware routing: automatically route INT8/batched embedding jobs to T4-equivalent runners when latency tolerance > 200ms.
- Prefix/KV cache carve-out: reserve a small set of GPUs (4 x A100) with larger memory for hot-cache replicas to reduce repeated KV reconstruction.
- Canary timeline: 3-week staged rollout with monitoring and automatic rollback if latency deviation > 10%.

Next steps I suggest: 1) confirm the preferred tranche mix, 2) sign the amendment (I can send DocuSign), 3) schedule a 45-minute runbook walkthrough with Karthik for kernel placement.

Ben / Karthik / Vanessa — pinging you for pricing numbers, technical caveats, and any lane changes before I send this externally.

Best,
Hannah

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the detailed draft. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the attached usage CSV:

1) Burst window: our quarter-end surge historically happens in the first 10 days of each quarter (roughly +70% token volume). We need an easy path to double burst capacity for 48 hours without a manual support ticket.
2) Latency tiers: we have two mission-critical surfaces — web chat (p95 target < 120ms) and batch embeddings (p95 unconstrained but cost sensitive).
3) KV cache behavior: we can expose the hot-key list for the month — that would help you size the cache replicas.

On approvals: procurement prefers a 90-day window to sign if we see the DocuSign with pricing + an explicit refund/rollback clause for early termination.

Can you also include a short note on how kernel-aware routing impacts model parity? Some of our models rely on fused attention kernels and we want to avoid regressions.

Sofia Martin

Following up with proposed commercial options to match the technical proposal. Two options that reflect Tailwind's mix of latency-critical and batch workloads:

Option A — Predictable steady state (recommended):
- 12 H100 reserved (monthly committed) for p95 < 120ms workloads.
- 24 A100 shared tranche for batch + finetunes (discounted at 18% off list).
- Burst buffer: 12 ephemeral slots billed at lower committed rates when used within the quarterly burst window.
- 12-month term with a 60% usage-rollback credit mechanism if committed utilization < 60% after 6 months.

Option B — Flex-first (lower upfront):
- 8 H100 reserved + 36 A100 flex (higher burst capacity but slightly higher unit cost).
- 6-month initial term with an automatic reprice at 6 months based on actual utilization.

Notes: procurement clause for a 90-day review window is ok; we'll add explicit rollback/refund language for early termination (legal to draft).

If Tailwind wants to guarantee the double-burst 48-hour window, we can formalize that as a reserved burst tranche with a scheduled activation API (we can limit activations per quarter to control capacity).

Technical notes on kernel-aware routing and model parity:

- Kernel families: our runtime tags kernels by numeric fidelity (FP16-HIGH, FP16-STABLE, INT8-FAST). We only route to INT8-FAST when the model checkpoint has been validated for equality at an acceptable divergence threshold. For proprietary fused-attention kernels, we will default to FP16-HIGH on H100-class hardware.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallbacks to a higher-fidelity kernel are synchronous and add ~15-30ms tail latency for in-flight requests; we'll keep H100s for the low-latency tier to avoid this.
- Cache sizing: based on tailwind_usage_q1_q2.csv, hot-key convergence suggests 3.6GB of pinned KV per replica; I recommend 4 replicas on A100(80GB) or 2 replicas on H100(80GB) with a read-only sticky routing to reduce cross-host fetches.
- Scheduling: we can implement a canary that pins 2 H100 slots and 6 A100 slots with traffic split 90/10 for the first week; if model metrics (latency, exact-match) stay within thresholds, we expand.

Operational caveats: quantization can reduce cost by ~30% on batch workloads but requires a 2-week validation window per model. We should include that validation step in the rollout timeline.
